# Self-study: Inline completions {.unnumbered} Inline completion is the simplest kind of assistantAny AI tool that helps you write or understand code, from inline completion to a chat window. In this course “assistant” is the general word; “agent” is used when the tool acts on your files.: grey "ghost text" appears as you type, and you accept it with Tab, reject it with Esc, or carry on typing. By the end of this page you will know how to get useful suggestions every time: write a specific comment just before the cursor. Claude Code has no inline completion, so this page uses GitHub Copilot instead. *Self-study: about 25 minutes, after the workshop day.* **Start state:** your workshop repository on `main`, Git pane clean, signed in to GitHub Copilot (if you are not, do the GitHub Copilot step in [Setting up Claude Code](11a-setup-claude-code.qmd) first). :::{#completions-files .callout-note collapse="true"} ## This page's files, and how it fits You work in the same **workshop repository** ([Setting up Claude Code](11a-setup-claude-code.qmd#your-workshop-repository)), with the same voles data, but not with Claude Code. GitHub Copilot is needed only for this page; Copilot Free is enough. The code you write here is practice, so it goes in `scratch/`, a folder git ignores: your Git pane stays clean, and there is no checkpoint branch, because nothing else depends on this code. | File | Where it comes from | Used in | |---|---|---| | `data/raw/voles_metabolism.csv` | Shipped with the template: 72 voles, 24 per treatment arm, one missing `metabolic_rate_post` | Both activities | | `scratch/completions.R` | You create it, in [the first activity](#completions-setup), step 0 | Both activities | ::: ## Activity: The context demonstration {#completions-setup} :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} The context demonstration (10 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **Goal:** see how the code above the cursor changes Copilot's suggestion for the same comment, so that you know what to put in a script to get useful suggestions. **Start state:** your workshop repository open, signed in to GitHub Copilot. The data are `voles_metabolism.csv`: a synthetic trial in 72 voles, with columns `subject_id`, `sex`, `treatment_arm`, `mass_pre_g`, `mass_post_g` and `metabolic_rate_post`. The names were chosen so that no model has seen them before. **0. Check that Copilot works.** This command creates the `scratch/` folder and this page's practice script, and opens it: **In the R console:** ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} usethis::edit_file("scratch/completions.R") ``` ::: In `scratch/completions.R`, type `# Calculate the mean of 1 to 100`. Within a few seconds you should see ghost text such as `mean(1:100)`; if not, press Enter and wait. **1. No context.** Delete everything in `scratch/completions.R`. Type only this comment, and wait. **In `scratch/completions.R`:** ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # calculate the mean change in mass by treatment ``` ::: Note the suggestion. With no data and no column names in view, the model has to guess. **2. Context in the file.** Empty `scratch/completions.R` again. Type the lines below down to `glimpse(voles)`, and run them, so that `voles` is loaded. Then type the same comment on a new line, and wait. **In `scratch/completions.R`:** ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # Voles metabolism trial: effect of treatment on body mass # 72 voles, three treatment arms (Control, Low_dose, High_dose), two sexes # Native pipe |>, tidyverse library(tidyverse) voles <- read_csv(here::here("data", "raw", "voles_metabolism.csv")) glimpse(voles) # calculate the mean change in mass by treatment ``` :::
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} voles |> mutate(mass_change_g = mass_post_g - mass_pre_g) |> summarise( mean_change = mean(mass_change_g, na.rm = TRUE), .by = treatment_arm ) ``` ::: The exact form varies between people and sessions.
Compare the two suggestions. Did the second use real column names? Did it compute post minus pre? **You are done when** you can say what the second suggestion had that the first did not. **If it goes wrong:** if no ghost text appears, check that you are signed in to GitHub and the set-up route for your IDE (in *Set-up routes, plans and data*, just after this task), then type the comment again on a new line; if `scratch/completions.R` stops running, *Session → Restart R* and run it from the top. :::: ::: :::{.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Set-up routes, plans and data - **RStudio:** enable GitHub Copilot in RStudio's options and sign in to GitHub. - **Positron:** choose GitHub Copilot as the completions provider (see Positron's completions documentation). Copilot Free allows a limited number of completions per month (2,000 at the time of writing); paid plans do not meter them. Completions send the code around your cursor to the provider, so the disclosure points in [Block 3](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd) apply here too. ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Using another tool Use one completion provider at a time, so you know which tool made each suggestion. **Posit AI Next Edit Suggestions** (RStudio and Positron): in RStudio, turn it on from the Posit Assistant toolbar button (it needs a Posit AI account); in Positron, choose it as the completions provider. Posit AI does not meter completions. Unlike Copilot, it also sees your live R session: the columns of loaded data frames, the functions you have defined and the packages you have loaded. So, in the context demonstration: - restart R (*Session → Restart R*) before step 1, so that "no context" means none; - after step 2, keep `voles` loaded, empty `scratch/completions.R` and type only the comment from step 1. If the suggestion now uses the real column names, they came from your session, not from the file. **VS Code:** select **Use AI Features** from the Copilot icon in the Status Bar and sign in with GitHub. As in Positron, Copilot may also use other open tabs. ::: ## The context principle A suggestion can only use what is in the model's context windowThe maximum amount of text a language model can consider in one call. The model has no memory between calls, so it sees only what is in the context window. when it is made. Copilot fills that window mainly from the current file, and above all from the comment just before the cursor. In Positron it may also use other open tabs. It does not see your R session. ## Activity: Build a small analysis :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Build a small analysis (10 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **Goal:** extend `scratch/completions.R` into a short analysis that reruns, deciding on every suggestion yourself, so that no suggestion enters your code unchecked. **Start state:** `scratch/completions.R` with the step 2 code from the demonstration, and `voles` loaded. For each step, write the comment first, then accept, modify or reject the suggestion, and note which you did in a comment under the code, for example `# modified: added n()`. The note is what makes you notice an unchecked acceptance. **0. Derived column.** Add `mass_change_g` (`mass_post_g` minus `mass_pre_g`) to `voles` as a column. Steps 1 and 2 need it there, not only inside a summary. **1. Summary table.** The mean and standard deviation of `mass_change_g` by `treatment_arm` and `sex`, with the number of observations per cell. **2. Plot.** `mass_change_g` against `metabolic_rate_post`, coloured by `treatment_arm`. **You are done when** steps 0 to 2 each have a note (accepted, modified or rejected), and `scratch/completions.R`, saved and run from the top in a fresh R sessionAn R session with nothing loaded from earlier work: Session > Restart R in RStudio or Positron (with “never save .RData” set, as on Day 1), callr::rscript() from the console, or Rscript in the terminal. Code that only works in your current session depends on something you did not record. (*Session → Restart R*), produces the table and the plot without error. **If it goes wrong:** delete the last suggestion you accepted, and write a more specific comment naming the data frame and its columns.
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # Voles metabolism trial: effect of treatment on body mass library(tidyverse) library(here) voles <- read_csv( here("data", "raw", "voles_metabolism.csv"), col_types = cols( subject_id = col_character(), sex = col_character(), treatment_arm = col_character(), mass_pre_g = col_double(), mass_post_g = col_double(), metabolic_rate_post = col_double() ) ) |> mutate(mass_change_g = mass_post_g - mass_pre_g) # mean and SD of mass_change_g by treatment_arm and sex, with n per cell voles |> summarise( mean_change_g = mean(mass_change_g), sd_change_g = sd(mass_change_g), n = n(), .by = c(treatment_arm, sex) ) |> arrange(treatment_arm, sex) # mass_change_g against metabolic_rate_post, coloured by treatment_arm ggplot(voles, aes(metabolic_rate_post, mass_change_g, colour = treatment_arm)) + geom_point() + labs(x = "Metabolic rate (post-treatment)", y = "Change in mass (g)") ``` ::: The plot drops the one animal with no metabolic rate and says so in a warning: read it rather than ignore it.
:::: ::: :::{.callout-note} ## Check · Reproduce · Record - **You can now:** steer inline completion with a specific comment and the right code above the cursor, **trusted because** you decided on every suggestion and your script runs from a fresh R session. - **Check:** accept, modify or reject every suggestion deliberately. - **Reproduce:** good suggestions come from context in the file, so keep that context in your script, where it reruns. - **Record:** nothing to log for practice code in `scratch/`. When completions write code you keep, add a line to your AI-use logA record written at the time of each piece of AI-assisted work, in the form: date; tool and model; task; what you kept or changed. It becomes the AI declaration in a README., in the form from [Block 3](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd). ::: ## Check your understanding **The single most reliable way to improve inline suggestions in a new script is to:**

## Going further This material goes beyond the two activities. Work through it if it is useful to you. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## The full four-step analysis The second activity leaves out the filter in step 1 and the model in step 3. The full sequence, again writing the comment for each step before accepting, rejecting or modifying the suggestion: 1. Filter to subjects with non-missing `metabolic_rate_post` and create a derived variable `mass_change_g`. 2. Produce a summary table of the mean and standard deviation of `mass_change_g` by `treatment_arm` and `sex`, with the number of observations per cell. 3. Fit a linear model of `metabolic_rate_post` on `treatment_arm` and `sex`. Inspect the coefficients. 4. Produce one plot relating `mass_change_g` to `metabolic_rate_post`, coloured by `treatment_arm`. When you have finished steps 2 and 4, compare the code you kept for step 4 with the plot in *An example* in the second activity, and note whether you accepted, changed or rejected Copilot's suggestion. Where the two differ, decide which is right and why: suggestions differ between people and between attempts, and so, often, do their bugs. If a colleague has worked through the same steps, compare your code with theirs too. ::: ## Glossary ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
term definition
AI-use log A record written at the time of each piece of AI-assisted work, in the form: date; tool and model; task; what you kept or changed. It becomes the AI declaration in a README.
assistant Any AI tool that helps you write or understand code, from inline completion to a chat window. In this course "assistant" is the general word; "agent" is used when the tool acts on your files.
context window The maximum amount of text a language model can consider in one call. The model has no memory between calls, so it sees only what is in the context window.
fresh R session An R session with nothing loaded from earlier work: Session > Restart R in RStudio or Positron (with "never save .RData" set, as on Day 1), callr::rscript() from the console, or Rscript in the terminal.
